memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Tell the whole community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man
is to take a lamb for his family, one for each household. If any household is
too small for a whole lamb, they must share one with their nearest neighbor,
having taken into account the number of people there are. You are to determine
the amount of lamb needed in accordance with what each person will eat."
- Ex 12:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives careful, practical instructions, and they are full of tenderness.

Notice first that the lamb is taken for the household. Salvation in Scripture is
deeply personal, but it is never meant to be private. Fathers were to act for
their families. This does not mean anyone is saved by another's faith, but it
does show God's heart for households. Later we see the same pattern with the
jailer at Philippi: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and
your household" (Acts 16:31).

Notice second the care for the small household. If your family is too small for
a whole lamb, share with your neighbour. Nobody is left out because they are few
or poor. The provision is measured according to what each person will eat, so
that there is enough and nothing is wasted.

This is the character of God on display in the details. He is not only planning
a nation's escape; He is thinking about the widow next door with two children
and no way to use a whole lamb.

The God who counted heads in Goshen still counts. He knows the exact size of
your need.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who in your circle is being left out because they are few or overlooked?
2. Have you taken spiritual responsibility for those in your household?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You notice the small and the overlooked. Help me to carry
my household before You in prayer and to make room for my neighbour. Amen.
